title: Tokens with a no-op fallback function can be used to steal the ETH balance of `LP`
summary: ## Severity  **Impact:** High, because it can lead to stolen funds from the protocol  **Likelihood:** Low, as it requires a token with a fallback function but without a `withdraw` function  ## Description  In `LP::withdrawPayout` we have the following code:  ```solidty if (isNative) {     IWNative(token).withdraw(amount);     TransferHelper.safeTransferETH(account, amount); } else {     TransferHelper.safeTransfer(token, account, amount); } ```  Now imagine the following scenario:  1. The `token` used in the contract is one that does not have a `withdraw` function but has a fallback function 2
